  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">January 14, 2022, was the record date with respect to the distribution of five-year listed warrants (the &#8220;Series A Warrants&#8221;).&#160; The Series A Warrants and the shares of common stock issuable upon the exercise of the Series A Warrants were registered on a registration statement that was filed with the SEC and was declared effective January 21, 2022. The Series A Warrants commenced trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol &#8220;SQFTW&#8221; on January 24, 2022 and were distributed on that date to persons who held shares of common stock and existing outstanding warrants as of the January 14, 2022 record date, or who acquired shares of common stock in the market following the record date, and who continued to hold such shares at the close of trading on January 21, 2022.&#160;The Series A Warrants give the holder the right to purchase one share of common stock at $70.00 per share, for a period of five years. Should warrant holders not exercise the Series A Warrants during that holding period, the Series A Warrants will automatically convert to 1/100 of a common share at expiration, rounded down to the nearest number of whole shares.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Series A Warrants:</i>&#160;If all the potential Series A Warrants outstanding at December 31, 2025, were exercised at the price of $70.00 per share, gross proceeds to us would be approximately $101.2&#160;million and we would as a result issue an additional 1,445,007&#160;shares of common stock.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Inflation</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The current inflationary environment has affected U.S. consumers and the repercussions may persist. As evidenced by the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI), a gauge employed by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, there was a 2.7% (not seasonally adjusted) increase for the 12-month period ending December&#160;31, 2025. The CPI serves as a metric for capturing the average fluctuations in prices paid by urban consumers across a diverse array of consumer goods and services. The macroeconomic landscape, including ongoing conflicts around the world, introduces an additional layer of complexity to the inflationary dynamics. These geopolitical disruptions have the potential to intensify inflationary pressures, contributing to the volatility witnessed in the broader economic context. As consumers navigate this challenging landscape, the potential for continued impact on their purchasing power remains a significant consideration.</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Leases generally provide for limited increases in rent as a result of fixed increases, increases in the consumer price index, or increases in clients&#8217; sales volumes. We expect that inflation will cause these lease provisions to result in rent increases over time. During times when inflation is greater than increases in rent, as provided for in the leases, rent increases may not keep up with the rate of inflation and other costs.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Moreover, our strategic focus on the use of net lease agreements reduces our exposure to rising property expenses due to inflation because the client is responsible for property expenses. Even though the utilization of net leases reduces our exposure to rising property expenses due to inflation, substantial inflationary pressures and increased costs may have an adverse impact on our clients if increases in their operating expenses exceed increases in revenue, which may adversely affect our clients' ability to pay rent. Additionally, inflationary periods may cause us to experience increased costs of financing, make it difficult to refinance debt at attractive rates or at all, and may adversely affect the properties we can acquire if the cost of financing an acquisition is in excess of our anticipated earnings from such property, thereby limiting the properties that can be acquired.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><a id="quanqual" title="quanqual" href="#"></a>ITEM 7A. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As a smaller reporting company, we are not required to provide disclosure pursuant to this item.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><a id="conpros" title="conpros" href="#"></a>ITEM 9A. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">We maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our Exchange Act reports is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to Management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure based closely on the definition of &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures&#8221; in Rule 13a-14(c). In designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, Management recognized that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives, and Management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible controls and procedures.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">As of the end of the period covered by this report, we carried out an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of our Management, including our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures. Based upon that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of the end of the period covered by this report.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting. Furthermore, we do not believe that these controls have been impacted by COVID-19 related circumstances, including remote work arrangements with our employees.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">Our Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(f). Under the supervision and with the participation of our Management, including our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework in Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 Framework). Based on our evaluation under the framework in Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework, our Management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">This annual report on Form 10-K does not include an attestation report of the Company&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm regarding our internal control over financial reporting as such report is not required for the Company.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><a id="directors" title="directors" href="#"></a>ITEM <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558546">10.</span> DIRECTORS, EXECUTIVE OFFICERS AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Except as set forth below, the information required by this item is set forth under the captions &#8220;Board of Directors&#8221; and &#8220;Executive Officers of the Company&#8221; and &#8220;Section <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>(a) Beneficial Ownership Reporting Compliance&#8221; in our definitive Proxy Statement for the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;Annual Meeting of Stockholders, to be filed with the SEC within <em style="font: inherit;">120</em> days of the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> pursuant to Regulation <em style="font: inherit;">14A,</em> and is incorporated herein by reference.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Insider Trading Policy</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has adopted an insider trading policy governing the purchase, sale, and/or other disposition of its securities by its directors, officers, employees and independent contractors that the Company believes is reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules and regulations, and the exchange listing standards applicable to the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Directors, executive officers, employees and other related persons <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> buy, sell or engage in other transactions in the Company&#8217;s shares while aware of material non-public information; buy or sell securities of other companies while aware of material non-public information about those companies that they became aware of as a result of business dealings between the Company and those companies; or disclose material non-public information to any unauthorized persons outside of the Company. The&#160;policy&#160;also restricts trading and other transactions for a limited group of Company employees (including executives and directors) to defined window periods that follow the Company's quarterly earnings releases and restricts trading and other transactions following announcement of a share repurchase program. A copy of such policy is filed hereto as Exhibit <em style="font: inherit;">19.1.</em></p>
  </div>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Opinion on the Financial Statements</i></b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Presidio Property Trust, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), as of December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, the related consolidated statements of operations, equity, and cash flows for the years then ended, and the related notes and financial statement Schedule III &#8211; Real Estate and Accumulated Depreciation and Amortization (collectively referred to as the &#8220;consolidated financial statements&#8221;). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of the Company as of December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, and the consolidated results of its operations and its cash flows for the years then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Basis for Opinion</i></b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#8220;PCAOB&#8221;) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits, we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated<i> </i>financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures to respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated<i> </i>financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements. We believe that our audits provides<i> </i>a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Critical Audit Matter</i></b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current period audit of the consolidated financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the consolidated financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. The communication of critical audit matters does not alter in any way our opinion on the consolidated financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matter below, providing a separate opinion on the critical audit matter or on the accounts or disclosures to which it relates.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Impairment of Real Estate Assets, net</i></b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">The Company&#8217;s real estate assets, inclusive of real estate assets held for sale, totaled approximately $108.6 million as of December 31, 2025. As more fully described in Note 2 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company reviews its real estate assets for impairment on a property-by-property basis. Impairment is recognized on a property held for use when the expected undiscounted cash flows for a property are less than the carrying amount at which time the property is written down to fair value. Determining fair value requires management to make estimates of future cash flows, which are based on a number of inputs and assumptions, including the terminal capitalization rate. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded approximately $6.4 million of impairment related to certain real estate assets.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">We identified the auditing of the Company&#8217;s impairment assessment for certain real estate assets as a critical audit matter. Auditing the Company&#8217;s impairment assessment for certain real estate assets is especially challenging due to the high degree of auditor judgement, subjectivity, and effort, including the need to involve our valuation specialists, in evaluating management&#8217;s estimated fair values for certain real estate assets.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">Addressing the matter involved performing procedures and evaluating audit evidence in connection with forming our overall opinion on the consolidated financial statements. Our audit procedures related to the impairment of certain real estate assets included the following, among others:</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:34pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Testing the mathematical accuracy of the valuation models for certain real estate assets.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:34pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Involving our valuation professionals with specialized skills and knowledge in (1) evaluating the reasonableness of the valuation methodology and (2) assessing the reasonableness of the terminal capitalization rate by comparing to independent market data.</p> </td></tr>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>Presidio Property Trust, Inc. and Subsidiaries</b></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"><em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> ORGANIZATION AND BASIS OF PRESENTATION</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Organization</span></i></b><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">. Presidio Property Trust, Inc. (&#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;our&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is an internally-managed real estate investment trust (&#8220;REIT&#8221;), with holdings in office, industrial, retail and model home properties. We were incorporated in the State of California on <em style="font: inherit;"> September&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">28,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">1999,</em> and in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2010, </em>we reincorporated as a Maryland corporation. In <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2017, </em>we changed our name from &#8220;NetREIT, Inc.&#8221; to &#8220;Presidio Property Trust, Inc.&#8221; Through Presidio Property Trust, Inc., its subsidiaries, and its partnerships, we own&#160;</span><ix:nonFraction id="c142558560" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-CommercialPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstatePropertiesFeeSimple" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;commercial properties in fee interest, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558561">two</span>&#160;of which we own as a partial interest in various affiliates, in which we serve as general partner, member and/or manager, and&#160;</span><ix:nonFraction id="c142558562" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">80</ix:nonFraction>&#160;model home residential properties<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> as noted below.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company or <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of its affiliates operates the following partnerships during the periods covered by these consolidated financial statements:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company is the sole general partner and limited partner in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558564">two</span> limited partnerships (NetREIT Palm Self-Storage LP and NetREIT Casa Grande LP), both of which, at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, had ownership interests in an entity that owns income producing real estate. The Company refers to these entities collectively as the "NetREIT Partnerships".</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company is the general and limited partner in <ix:nonFraction id="c142558565" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfLimitedPartnershipsInWhichCompanyIsSoleGeneralPartner" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">six</ix:nonFraction> limited partnerships that purchase model homes and lease them back to homebuilders as commercial tenants (Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#202,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#203,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#204,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#205,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#206,</em> LP, and Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#207,</em> LP). As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#202,</em> LP, Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#203,</em> LP and Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">#206,</em> LP had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> remaining assets.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has determined that the limited partnerships in which it owns less than <em style="font: inherit;">100%</em> should be included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements as the Company directs their activities and has control of such limited partnerships.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have elected to be taxed as a REIT under Sections <em style="font: inherit;">856</em> through <em style="font: inherit;">860</em> of the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;), for federal income tax purposes.&#160;To maintain our qualification as a REIT, we are required to distribute at least <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of our REIT taxable income to our stockholders and meet the various other requirements imposed by the Code relating to such matters as operating results, asset holdings, distribution levels, and diversity of stock ownership. Provided we maintain our qualification for taxation as a REIT, we are generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to corporate-level income tax on the earnings distributed currently to our stockholders that we derive from our REIT&#160;qualifying activities. If we fail to maintain our qualification as a REIT in any taxable year and are unable to avail ourselves of certain savings provisions set forth in the Code, all our taxable income would be subject to federal income tax at regular corporate rates, including any applicable alternative minimum tax. We are subject to certain state and local income taxes.</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
     &#160;
   </div>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We, together with <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of our entities, have elected to treat certain subsidiaries as a taxable REIT subsidiary (a &#8220;TRS&#8221;) for federal income tax purposes. Certain activities that we undertake must be conducted by a TRS, such as non-customary services for our commercial tenants, and holding assets that we cannot hold directly. A TRS is subject to federal and state income taxes. The Company has concluded that there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition in its financial statements. Neither the Company nor its subsidiaries have been assessed any significant interest or penalties for tax positions by any&#160;tax jurisdictions.</p>

   <p style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff">Liquidity.</span></i></b><span style="background-color:#ffffff">&#160;</span>The Company's anticipated future sources of liquidity <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include existing cash and cash equivalents, cash flows from operations, refinancing of existing mortgages, future real estate sales, new borrowings, and the sale of equity or debt securities.&#160;Future capital needs include paying down existing borrowings, maintaining our existing properties, funding tenant improvements on our commercial buildings, paying lease commissions (to the extent they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> covered by lender-held reserve deposits), and the payment of dividends to our stockholders. The Company is also seeking investments that are likely to produce income and achieve long-term gains in order to pay dividends to our stockholders. To ensure that we can effectively execute these objectives, we routinely review our liquidity requirements and continually evaluate all potential sources of liquidity. If necessary, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>seek other short-term liquidity alternatives, such as bridge loans, refinancing an unencumbered property or a bank line&#160;of credit depending on&#160;the credit environment.&#160;See note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>&#160;Stockholders' Equity for additional information on sale of securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Short-term liquidity needs include paying our current operating costs, satisfying the debt service requirements of existing mortgages, completing tenant improvements on our commercial buildings, paying leasing commissions, distributions to non-controlling interests, and funding dividends, if any, to stockholders.&#160;Future principal payments due on mortgage notes payables, during&#160;<span style="background-color:#ffffff">the&#160;year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2026</em></span>&#160;total approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558588" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-MortgageNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">30.0</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;<span style="background-color:#ffffff">of which&#160;</span>$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558589" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-MortgageNotesMember_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtMaturitiesRepaymentsOfPrincipalInNextTwelveMonths" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.5</ix:nonFraction> million<span style="background-color:#ffffff">&#160;is related to model home properties.</span>&#160;See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em> Mortgage Notes Payable for additional information on the Dakota Center and Shea Center II loans.&#160;Management expects certain model home properties can be sold, and that the underlying mortgage notes will be paid off with sales proceeds while other mortgage notes can be refinanced, as the Company has&#160;historically&#160;been able to do in&#160;the past with all model home properties. Additional principal payments will be made with cash flows from ongoing operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As the Company continues its operations, it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>re-finance or seek additional financing. However, there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that any such re-financing or additional financing will be available to the Company on acceptable terms, if at all. If events or circumstances occur such that the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obtain additional funding, it will most likely be required to reduce its plans and/or certain discretionary spending, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company's ability to achieve its intended business objectives. Management believes that the combination of working capital on hand and the ability to refinance commercial and model home mortgages will fund operations through at least the next <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months from the date of the issuance of these unaudited interim financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Segments. </i></b>The Company acquires and operates income producing properties in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558594">three</span> business segments including Office/Industrial Properties, Model Home Properties and Retail Properties. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> &#8220;Segments&#8221;.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Concentration. </i></b>Concentration of credit risk with respect to tenant receivables is limited due to the large number of tenants comprising the Company&#8217;s rental revenue.&#160;We have <ix:nonFraction id="c142558596" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_StatementGeographicalAxis-CO" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">three</ix:nonFraction> commercial properties located in Colorado, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558597">four</span> in North Dakota,&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558598">one</span> in Southern California, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558599">one</span> in Texas and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558600">one</span> in Maryland. Our model home properties are concentrated in Texas with a few model homes in Tennessee and Arizona.&#160;We had <ix:nonFraction id="c142558601" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-RentalIncomeMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfTenants" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> tenant account for&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142558602" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-RentalIncomeMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OneTenantMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">6.90</ix:nonFraction>% of base rental income for commercial properties for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. Conversely, <ix:nonFraction id="c142558603" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-SalesRevenueNetMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfHomebuilders" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> of our homebuilders&#160;accounts for approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142558604" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-SalesRevenueNetMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OneHomebuilderMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">15.9</ix:nonFraction>% of our total revenue for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and accounted for <ix:nonFraction id="c142558605" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember_ShareBasedGoodsAndNonemployeeServicesTransactionBySupplierAxis-OneHomebuilderMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">56</ix:nonFraction> out of <ix:nonFraction id="c142558606" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomePropertiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">80</ix:nonFraction> of our model home leases as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em> SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559524" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Basis of Presentation. </i></b>The accompanying financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) as contained within the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559525" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Principles of Consolidation</i></b>. The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Presidio Property Trust, Inc. and its subsidiaries, NetREIT Advisors, LLC and Dubose Advisors LLC (collectively, the &#8220;Advisors&#8221;), and NetREIT Dubose Model Home REIT, Inc. The consolidated&#160;financial statements also include the results of the NetREIT Partnerships and&#160;the Model Home Partnerships.&#160;As used herein, references to the &#8220;Company&#8221; include references to Presidio Property Trust, Inc., its subsidiaries, and the partnerships. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company classifies the noncontrolling interests in the NetREIT Partnerships as part of consolidated net (loss) income&#160;in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and has included the accumulated amount of noncontrolling interests as part of equity since inception in <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2010. </em>If a change in ownership of a consolidated subsidiary results in loss of control and deconsolidation, any retained ownership interest will be remeasured, with the gain or loss reported in the consolidated statements of operations. Management has evaluated the noncontrolling interests and determined that they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain any redemption features.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c142559526" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b>. The&#160;consolidated financial statements were prepared in conformity with U.S. GAAP, which requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period. Significant estimates include, private warrants,&#160;the allocation of purchase price paid for property acquisitions between the components of land, building and intangible assets acquired including their useful lives,&#160;valuation of long-lived assets, and the allowance for doubtful accounts, which is based on an evaluation of the tenants&#8217; ability to pay. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RealEstatePolicyTextBlock" id="c142559527" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Real Estate Assets and Lease Intangibles. </i></b>Land, buildings and improvements are recorded at cost, including tenant improvements and lease acquisition costs (including leasing commissions, space planning fees, and legal fees). The Company capitalizes any expenditure that replaces, improves, or otherwise extends the economic life of an asset, while ordinary repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred. The Company allocates the purchase price of acquired properties between the acquired tangible assets and liabilities (consisting of land, buildings, tenant improvements, and long-term debt) and identified intangible assets and liabilities (including the value of above-market and below-market leases, the value of in-place leases, unamortized lease origination costs and tenant relationships), in each case based on their respective fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company allocates the purchase price to tangible assets of an acquired property based on the estimated fair values of those tangible assets, assuming the property was vacant. Estimates of fair value for land, building and building improvements are based on many factors, including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, comparisons to other properties sold in the same geographic area and independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuations. In estimating the fair values of the tangible assets, intangible assets, and liabilities acquired, the Company also considers information obtained about each property as a result of its pre&#8209;acquisition due diligence, marketing and leasing activities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The value allocated to acquired lease intangibles is based on management&#8217;s evaluation of the specific characteristics of each tenant&#8217;s lease. Characteristics considered by management in allocating these values include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited, to the nature and extent of the existing business relationships with the tenant, growth prospects for developing new business with the tenant, the remaining term of the lease,&#160;the tenant&#8217;s credit quality, and other factors.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The value attributable to the above-market or below-market component of an acquired&#160;in-place lease is determined based upon the present value (using a market discount rate) of the difference between (i) the contractual rents to be paid pursuant to the lease over its remaining term, and (ii) management&#8217;s estimate of rents that would be paid using fair market rates over the remaining term of the lease. The amounts allocated to above or below-market leases are amortized on a straight-line basis as an increase or reduction of rental income over the remaining non-cancelable term of the respective leases. Amortization of above and below-market rents resulted in a net increase in rental income of approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558615" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfAboveAndBelowMarketLeases" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4,753</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558616" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfAboveAndBelowMarketLeases" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4,641</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The value of in-place leases and unamortized lease origination costs are amortized to expenses over the remaining term of the respective leases, which range from less than a year to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558618">ten</span> years. The amount allocated to acquired in-place leases is determined based on management&#8217;s assessment of lost revenue and costs incurred for the period required to lease the &#8220;assumed vacant&#8221; property to the occupancy level when purchased. The amount allocated to unamortized lease origination costs is determined by what the Company would have paid to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party to secure a new tenant reduced by the expired term of the respective lease. The amount allocated to tenant relationships is the benefit resulting from the likelihood of a tenant renewing its lease. Amortization expense related to these assets was approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558620" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-LeaseAgreementsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">15,670</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558621" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-LeaseAgreementsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">17,526</ix:nonFraction> for years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RealEstateHeldForDevelopmentAndSalePolicy" id="c142559528" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Real Estate Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations.</i></b>&#160;We generally reclassify assets to "held for sale" when the disposition has been approved, it is available for immediate sale in its present condition, we are actively&#160;seeking a buyer, and the disposition is considered probable within <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year.&#160;Additionally, real estate sold during the current period is classified as &#8220;real estate assets held for sale&#8221; for all prior periods presented in the accompanying&#160;consolidated financial statements. Mortgage notes payable related to the real estate sold during the current period are&#160;classified as &#8220;mortgage notes payable related to properties held for sale&#8221; for all prior periods presented in the accompanying&#160;consolidated financial statements.&#160;Additionally, we record the operating results related to real estate that has been disposed of as discontinued operations&#160;for all periods presented if the operations have been eliminated and represent a strategic shift and we will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any significant continuing involvement in the operations of the property following the sale.&#160;Properties considered held for sale are recorded at the lesser of the carrying value or fair value less costs to sell.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, only <ix:nonFraction id="c142558626" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-CommercialPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfPropertiesClassifiedAsHeldForSale" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> commercial property, Dakota Center, met the criteria to be classified as "held for sale," and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142558627" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomeMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfPropertiesClassifiedAsHeldForSale" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">five</ix:nonFraction>&#160;model homes were classified as "held for sale"&#160;but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered discontinued operations or a strategic shift in our operations.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559529" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Impairments of Real Estate Assets.&#160;</i></b>We regularly review for impairment on a property-by-property basis. Impairment is recognized on a property&#160;held for use when the expected undiscounted cash flows for a property are less than the carrying amount at which time the property is written-down to fair value. Impairment is recognized on a property held for sale when the fair value less costs to sell is less than the carrying amount. If the carrying amount exceeds the undiscounted cash flows, we calculate an impairment loss by comparing the carrying amount to estimated fair value, using discounted cash flow models or <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party appraisals. The calculation of both discounted and undiscounted cash flows requires management to make estimates of future cash flows that are determined based on a number of inputs and assumptions, including but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the terminal capitalization rate. Actual results could be significantly different from the estimates. Although our strategy is to hold our properties over the long-term, if our strategy changes or market conditions otherwise dictate an earlier sale date, an impairment loss <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be recognized to reduce the property to fair value and such loss could be material.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559530" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Intangible Assets</i></b>. Intangible assets, including goodwill and lease intangibles, are comprised of finite-lived and indefinite-lived assets. Lease intangibles represent&#160;the allocation of a portion of the purchase price of a property acquisition representing the estimated value of in-place leases, unamortized lease origination costs, tenant relationships and land purchase options. Intangible assets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deemed to have an indefinite useful life are amortized over their estimated useful lives. Indefinite-lived assets are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> amortized. Amortization&#160;expense of intangible assets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deemed to have an indefinite useful life was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558641" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558642" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and is included in depreciation and amortization in the accompanying consolidated statements of operation.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company is required to perform a test for impairment of goodwill and other definite and indefinite lived assets at least annually, and more frequently as circumstances warrant. Impairment is recognized only if the carrying amount of the intangible asset is considered to be unrecoverable from its undiscounted cash flows and is measured as the difference between the carrying amount and the estimated fair value of the asset. For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>we have recorded an impairment charge to the goodwill of NTR Property Management for approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558644" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ReportingUnitAxis-NtrPropertyManagementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">72,000</ix:nonFraction>.&#160;See <i>Fair Value Measurements </i>below for additional information.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DepreciationDepletionAndAmortizationPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559531" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Depreciation and Amortization. </i></b>The Company records depreciation and amortization expense using the straight-line method over the useful lives of the respective assets. The costs of buildings are depreciated over estimated useful lives of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-BuildingMember" name="us-gaap:RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationLifeUsedForDepreciation1" id="c142558645" format="ixt-sec:duryear">39</ix:nonNumeric> years, the costs of improvements are amortized over the shorter of the estimated life of the asset or term of the tenant lease (which range from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-LeaseholdImprovementsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationLifeUsedForDepreciation1" id="c142558646" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-LeaseholdImprovementsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationLifeUsedForDepreciation1" id="c142558647" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years), the costs associated with acquired tenant intangibles over the remaining lease term and the cost of furniture, fixtures and equipment are depreciated over <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-FurnitureAndFixturesMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationLifeUsedForDepreciation1" id="c142558648" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-FurnitureAndFixturesMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationLifeUsedForDepreciation1" id="c142558649" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric> years. Depreciation and amortization expense for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;was approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558651" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DepreciationAndAmortization" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.9</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558652" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DepreciationAndAmortization" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.5</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, and is included in depreciation and amortization in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559532" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Cash, Cash Equivalents and Restricted Cash.&#160;</i></b>At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, we had approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558653" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.4</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558654" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">8.0</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, respectively.&#160;The Company considers all short-term, highly liquid investments that are both readily convertible to cash and have an original maturity of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less at the date of purchase to be cash equivalents. Items classified as cash equivalents include money market funds. Cash balances in individual banks <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exceed the federally insured limit of <em style="font: inherit;">$250,000</em> by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC"). <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> losses have been experienced related to such accounts. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558658" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashUninsuredAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;in deposits in financial institutions that exceeded the federally insurable limits. Restricted cash consists of funds held in escrow for Company lenders for properties held as collateral by the lenders. The funds in escrow are for payment of property taxes, insurance, leasing costs, mortgage payment reserves,&#160;and capital expenditures. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company has approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558659" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.7</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;of restricted cash.&#160;At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, the Company had approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558660" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashUninsuredAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;in deposits in financial institutions that exceeded the federally insurable limits.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, the Company has approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558661" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;of restricted cash.</p>

     <b><i></i></b></div></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:TradeAndOtherAccountsReceivablePolicy" id="c142559533" escape="true"><div style="font-size:10pt"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Accounts Receivables. </i></b>The Company periodically evaluates the collectability of amounts due from tenants and maintains an allowance for doubtful accounts for estimated losses resulting from the inability of tenants to make required payments under lease agreements. In addition, the Company maintains an allowance for deferred rent receivable that arises from straight lining of rents. The Company exercises judgment in establishing these allowances and considers payment history and current credit status of its tenants in developing these estimates. As of
     <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and
     <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the balance of allowance for possible uncollectable tenant receivables included in other assets, net in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets was approximately&#160;
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558664" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivable" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558665" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivable" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.

     <b><i></i></b></div></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DeferredChargesPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559534" escape="true"><div style="font-size:10pt"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Deferred Leasing Costs. </i></b>Costs incurred in connection with successful property leases are capitalized as deferred leasing costs and amortized to leasing commission expense on a straight-line basis over the terms of the related leases which generally range from
     <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558666">one</span> to
     <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558667">five</span> years. Deferred leasing costs consist of
     <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party leasing commissions. Management re-evaluates the remaining useful lives of leasing costs as the creditworthiness of the tenants and economic and market conditions change. If management determines the estimated remaining life of the respective lease has changed, the amortization period is adjusted. At
     <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and
     <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company had net deferred leasing costs of approximately&#160;
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558670" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCostsCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and&#160;
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558671" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCostsCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.7</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. Total amortization expense for the years ended
     <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and
     <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;was approximately&#160;
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558673" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseInitialDirectCostExpenseOverTerm" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and&#160;
     $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558674" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseInitialDirectCostExpenseOverTerm" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, and is included in the total for depreciation and amortization noted above.

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Deferred Financing Costs. </i></b>Costs incurred, including legal fees, origination fees, and administrative fees, in connection with debt financing are capitalized as deferred financing costs, are amortized using the straight line method, which approximates the effective interest method, over the contractual term of the respective loans and recorded as an offset to the carrying value of the debt. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, unamortized deferred financing costs related to mortgage notes payable were approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558676" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-PolarMultiStrategyMasterFundMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558677" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-PolarMultiStrategyMasterFundMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, total amortization expense related to the mortgage notes payable deferred financing costs was approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558679" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-PolarMultiStrategyMasterFundMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">281,245</ix:nonFraction> and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558680" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-PolarMultiStrategyMasterFundMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-NotesPayableToBanksMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfFinancingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">351,291</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.<b><i>&#160;</i></b>Amortization of deferred financing costs are included in interest expense in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>Deferred Offering Costs.&#160;</b></i>Deferred offering costs represent legal, accounting and other direct costs related to our&#160;offerings. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, we have&#160;incurred approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558682" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredOfferingCosts" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">279,603</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559275">zero</span>, respectively, in deferred offering costs as of&#160;the end of each period related to our&#160;registration statement on Form S-<em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559535" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Income Taxes.</i></b>&#160;We have elected to be taxed as a REIT under Sections <em style="font: inherit;">856</em> through <em style="font: inherit;">860</em> of the Code, for federal income tax purposes.<b><i> </i></b>To maintain our qualification as a REIT, we are required to distribute at least <ix:nonFraction id="c142558686" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:PercentageOfDistributedTaxableIncomeToQualifyAsREIT" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% of our REIT taxable income to our stockholders and meet the various other requirements imposed by the Code relating to such matters as operating results, asset holdings, distribution levels and diversity of stock ownership. Provided we maintain our qualification for taxation as a REIT, we are generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to corporate level income tax on the earnings distributed currently to our stockholders that we derive from our REIT qualifying activities. If we fail to maintain our qualification as a REIT in any taxable year, and are unable to avail ourselves of certain savings provisions set forth in the Code, all of our taxable income would be subject to federal income tax at regular corporate rates, including any applicable alternative minimum tax. We are subject to certain state and local income taxes. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we have estimated&#160;approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558688" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="sqft:EstimatedFutureOperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">27.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of Federal net operating loss (NOLs) carryforwards to offset potential future federal tax obligations. We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> generate sufficient taxable income in future periods to be able to realize fully the tax benefits of our NOL carry-forwards.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We, together with <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of our entities, have elected to treat certain subsidiaries as a taxable REIT subsidiary (a &#8220;TRS&#8221;) for federal income tax purposes. Certain activities that we undertake must be conducted by a TRS, such as non-customary services for our tenants, and holding assets that we cannot hold directly. A TRS is subject to federal and state income taxes. The Company has concluded that there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition in its financial statements. Neither the Company nor its subsidiaries have been assessed any significant interest or penalties for tax positions by any&#160;tax jurisdictions.</p>

     <b><i></i></b></div></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559536" escape="true"><div style="font-size:10pt"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Fair Value Measurements</i></b>.&#160;Certain assets and liabilities are required to be carried at fair value, or if long-lived assets are deemed to be impaired, to be adjusted to reflect this condition.
