   <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 2%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 2%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 96%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active, and model-derived valuations in which significant inputs and significant value drivers are observable in active markets; and</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 2%;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 2%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 96%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> prices or valuation techniques where little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market data is available that requires inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">When available, we utilize quoted market prices from independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party sources to determine fair value and classify such items in Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> or Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em><i>.</i>&#160;In instances where the market for a financial instrument is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;active, regardless of the availability of a nonbinding quoted market price, observable inputs might <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;be relevant and could require us to make a significant adjustment to derive a fair value measurement.&#160;Additionally, in an inactive market, a market price quoted from an independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party <em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>rely more on models with inputs based on information available only to that independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party. When we determine the market for a financial instrument owned by us to be illiquid or when market transactions for similar instruments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;appear orderly, we use several valuation sources (including internal valuations, discounted cash flow analysis and quoted market prices) and establish a fair value by assigning weights to the various valuation sources.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Additionally, in an inactive market, a market price quoted from an independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party <em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>rely more on models with inputs based on information available only to that independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party. When we determine the market for a financial instrument owned by us to be illiquid or when market transactions for similar instruments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;appear orderly, we use several valuation sources (including internal valuations, discounted cash flow analysis and quoted market prices) and establish a fair value by assigning weights to the various valuation sources.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558709">not</span> hold any&#160;marketable securities,&#160;excluding our investments in Conduit's common stock and common stock warrants.&#160;As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, our marketable securities&#160;(excluding our investments in Conduit's common stock and common stock warrants),&#160;held at a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party broker,&#160;presented on the&#160;consolidated balance sheets within other assets&#160;were measured at fair value using Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> market prices and totaled approximately&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142558712" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel1Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MarketableSecurities" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">zero</ix:nonFraction>, with a cost basis of approximately&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142558713" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="sqft:MarketableSecuritiesCostBasis" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">zero</ix:nonFraction>.&#160;There were <ix:nonFraction id="c142558714" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LiabilitiesFairValueDisclosure" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;financial liabilities measured at fair value as&#160;of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em><i>.</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 22, 2024, </em>the    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c142559537" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Earnings per share (</i></b>&#8220;<b><i>EPS</i></b>&#8221;<b><i>). </i></b>The EPS on common stock has been computed pursuant to the guidance in FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">260,</em> Earnings Per Share.&#160;The guidance requires the classification of the Company&#8217;s unvested restricted stock, which contains rights to receive non-forfeitable dividends, as participating securities requiring the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method of computing net income per share of common stock.&#160;In accordance with the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method, earnings per share have&#160;been computed by dividing the net income less net income attributable to unvested restricted shares by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding less unvested restricted shares. Diluted earnings per share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average shares of common stock and potentially dilutive securities outstanding in accordance with the treasury stock method.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Dilutive common stock equivalents include the dilutive effect of in-the-money stock equivalents, which are calculated based on the average share price for each period using the treasury stock method, excluding any common stock equivalents if their effect would be anti-dilutive. In periods in which a net loss has been incurred, all potentially dilutive common stock shares are considered anti-dilutive and thus are excluded from the calculation.&#160;Securities that are excluded from the calculation of weighted average dilutive common stock, because their inclusion would have been antidilutive, are:</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Income (Loss) per Common Share. </i></b>Basic income (loss) per common share (Basic EPS) is computed by dividing net income (loss) available to common shareholders (Numerator) by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding (Denominator) during the period. Diluted loss per common share (Diluted EPS) is similar to the computation of Basic EPS except that the Denominator is increased to include the number of additional common shares that would have been outstanding if the dilutive potential common shares had been issued. In addition, in computing the dilutive effect of convertible securities, the Numerator is adjusted to add back the after-tax amount of interest recognized in the period associated with any convertible debt. The computation of Diluted EPS does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> assume exercise or conversion of securities that would have an anti-dilutive effect on net loss per share.&#160;For the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the basic and diluted net loss per share was&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558742" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareBasic" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">8.65</ix:nonFraction>, since all&#160;potentially dilutive securities were determined to be anti-dilutive,&#160;and for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em> the basic and diluted net earnings per share are equivalent at&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558743" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareBasic" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">22.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per share because the Company had incurred a net loss attributable to common stockholders causing any potentially dilutive securities to be anti-dilutive.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559539" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Sales of Real Estate Assets</i></b>.&#160;Effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2018, </em>we adopted the guidance of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">610</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> Other Income - Gains and Losses from the Derecognition of Nonfinancial Assets (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">610</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20&#8221;</em>), which applies to sales or transfers to noncustomers of nonfinancial assets or in substance nonfinancial assets that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the definition of a business. Asset sales are generally recognized when control of the asset being sold is transferred to the buyer. As the assets are sold, their costs and related accumulated depreciation, if any, are derecognized with resulting gains or losses reflected in net income.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">610</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em> refers to the revenue recognition principles under ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2014</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">9.</em> Under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">610</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> if we determine we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a controlling financial interest in the entity that holds the asset and the arrangement meets the criteria to be accounted for as a contract, we would derecognize the asset and recognize a gain or loss on the sale of the real estate when control of the underlying asset transfers to the buyer.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Revenue Recognition and Accounts Receivables</i></b>. We recognize minimum rent, including rental abatements, lease incentives and contractual fixed increases attributable to operating leases, on a straight-line basis over the term of the related leases when collectability is probable and record amounts expected to be received in later years as deferred rent receivable. The cumulative difference between lease revenue recognized under the straight-line method and contractual lease payments are recorded as deferred rent receivable within other assets the consolidated balance sheets. Additionally, we recognize transaction fees associated with the leasing of our model homes&#160;on a straight-line basis over the term of the related leases and are&#160;included within rental income&#160;on our consolidated statement of operations.&#160;The Company&#8217;s lease revenue is impacted by the Company&#8217;s determination of whether improvements to the property, whether made by the Company or by the tenant, are landlord assets. The determination of whether an improvement is a landlord asset requires judgment. In making this judgment, the Company&#8217;s primary consideration is whether an improvement would be utilizable by another tenant upon the then-existing tenant vacating the improved space. If the Company has funded an improvement that it determines <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be landlord assets, then it treats the cost of the improvement as a lease incentive.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For certain leases, the Company also makes significant assumptions and judgments in determining the lease term. The lease term impacts the period over which the Company determines and records lease payments and also impacts the period over which it amortizes lease-related costs. The Company considers all relevant factors that create an economic incentive for the lessee and uses judgment to determine if those factors, considered together, signify that the lessee is reasonably certain to exercise the option.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We record property operating expense reimbursements due from tenants for common area maintenance, real estate taxes, and other recoverable costs in the period the related expenses are incurred.&#160;Additional rent where we pay the associated costs directly to <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party vendors and are reimbursed by our tenants are recognized and recorded on a gross basis, with the associated expense recognized in property expenses or real estate taxes.&#160;Because the timing and pattern of transferring rental revenue and related operating expense reimbursements to the lessee are the same, and our leases are classified as operating leases, we treat rental revenue and tenant recovery revenue as a single combined lease component. Accordingly, operating expense reimbursements are reported within Rental Income on the Company&#8217;s consolidated statement of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>

   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We make estimates of the collectability of our tenant receivables related to base rents, including deferred rent receivable, expense reimbursements and other revenue or income. We specifically analyze accounts receivable, deferred rent receivable, historical bad debts, customer creditworthiness, current economic trends and changes in customer payment terms when evaluating the adequacy of the allowance for doubtful accounts. In addition, with respect to tenants in bankruptcy, management makes estimates of the expected recovery of pre-petition and post-petition claims in assessing the estimated collectability of the related receivable. In some cases, the ultimate resolution of these claims can exceed <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year. When a tenant is in bankruptcy, we will record a bad debt reserve for the tenant&#8217;s receivable balance and generally will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize subsequent rental revenue until cash is received or until the tenant is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer in bankruptcy and has the ability to make rental payments.&#160;Fees and other income primarily include amounts recorded in connection with transient daily parking and miscellaneous amounts that fall within the scope of ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> Revenue from Contracts with Customers, and are recognized as revenue at the point in time when control of the goods or services transfers to the customer and our performance obligation is satisfied.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationVariableInterestEntityPolicy" id="c142559540" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Variable Interest Entity.</i></b>&#160;We determine whether an entity is a Variable Interest Entity ("VIE") and, if so, whether it should be consolidated by utilizing judgments and estimates that are inherently subjective. Our determination of whether an entity in which we hold a direct or indirect variable interest is a VIE is based on several factors, including whether we participated in the design of the entity and the entity&#8217;s total equity investment at risk upon inception is sufficient to finance the entity&#8217;s activities without additional subordinated financial support. We make judgments regarding the sufficiency of the equity at risk based <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> on a qualitative analysis, and then a quantitative analysis, if necessary.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We analyze any investments in VIEs to determine if we are the primary beneficiary. In evaluating whether we are the primary beneficiary, we evaluate our direct and indirect economic interests in the entity. A reporting entity is determined to be the primary beneficiary if it holds a controlling financial interest in the VIE. Determining which reporting entity, if any, has a controlling financial interest in a VIE is primarily a qualitative approach focused on identifying which reporting entity has both: (i) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact such entity&#8217;s economic performance; and (ii) the obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits from such entity that could potentially be significant to such entity. Performance of that analysis requires the exercise of judgment.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We consider a variety of factors in identifying the entity that holds the power to direct matters that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance, including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the ability to direct operating decisions and activities. In addition, we consider the rights of other investors to participate in those decisions. We determine whether we are the primary beneficiary of a VIE at the time we become involved with a variable interest entity and reconsider that conclusion continually.&#160;We consolidate any VIE of which we are the primary beneficiary.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

     <b><i></i></b></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:SubsequentEventsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559541" escape="true"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Subsequent Events. </i></b>We evaluate subsequent events up until the date the consolidated financial statements are issued.&#160;See note
     <em style="font: inherit;">16</em>&#160;Subsequent Events.

     <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142559542" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Recently Issued and Adopted Accounting Pronouncements.&#160;</i></b>In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em>&#160;<i>Income Taxes</i>, to enhance income tax disclosures, provide more information about tax risks and opportunities present in worldwide operations, and to disaggregate existing income tax disclosures. The guidance is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024 </em>on a prospective basis, with the option to apply the standard retrospectively. Early adoption is permitted. We have&#160;adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> and have updated our&#160;financial statement disclosures accordingly;&#160;there was <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material impact to our financial statement.</p>
     <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
     <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2024, </em>the SEC issued final climate-disclosure rules to enhance and standardize climate&#8208;related disclosures by public companies. With regards to financial statements, the rules requires disclosure of (i)&#160;capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions, subject to applicable <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> percent and de minimis disclosure thresholds; (ii)&#160;capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and renewable energy credits or certificates (RECs)&#160;if used as a material component of a company's plans to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals; and (iii) if the estimates and assumptions the company uses to produce the financial statements were materially impacted by risks and uncertainties associated with severe weather events and other natural conditions or any disclosed climate-related targets or transition plans, a qualitative description of how the development of such estimates and assumptions was impacted. The rules are effective for annual periods beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025 </em>and are to be applied prospectively. On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 4, 2024, </em>the SEC voluntarily stayed the rules pending judicial review as a result of litigation. On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2025, </em>the SEC voted to end its defense of the rules requiring disclosure of climate-related risks and greenhouse gas emissions.&#160;However, the Eighth Circuit <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>still rule on the legal challenges to the rules, and if so could decide to uphold the rules in whole or in part or remand them to the SEC for further consideration.</p>

     <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;<i>Income Statement</i>&#8212;<i>Reporting Comprehensive, Income</i>&#8212;<i>Expense Disaggregation Disclosures, Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>&#160;(&#8220;ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03&#8221;</em>).&#160;This ASU is to improve the disclosures about a public business entity&#8217;s expenses and address requests from investors for more detailed information about the types of expenses (including purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, amortization, and depletion) in commonly presented expense captions (such as cost of sales, SG&amp;A, and research and development).&#160;The amendments in this ASU are effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption is permitted.&#160;In <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2025, </em>this was updated by ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01&#8212;Income</em> Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Clarifying the Effective Date.&#160;The amendment in this Update amends the effective date of Update <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> to clarify that all public business entities are required to adopt the guidance in annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption of Update <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is permitted.&#160;We have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> and are currently evaluating the impact on our financial statement disclosures.</p>
     <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
     <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> - <i>Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>),</i> which focuses on improving interim reporting guidance by clarifying requirements and enhancing navigability for entities preparing interim financial statements under GAAP.&#160; This aims to improve the guidance in Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270,</em> Interim Reporting, by enhancing the clarity and navigability of the required interim disclosures. This introduces the Disclosure Principle, requiring entities to disclose events that have a material impact on the entity since the end of the last annual reporting period. Additionally, ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> creates a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures, consolidating them into Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em> rather than having them dispersed across various Codification Topics. For public entities, the update is effective for interim reporting periods within annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>For all other entities, it is effective for interim reporting periods within annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2028. </em>Early adoption is permitted for all entities. While we are currently evaluating the impact of this pronouncement, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect it will have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Periodically, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>sell an option in the marketable securities it holds to unrelated <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties for the right to purchase certain securities held within its investment portfolios (&#8220;covered call options&#8221;). These option transactions are designed primarily to increase the total return associated with holding the related securities as earning assets by using fee income generated from these options. These transactions are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging relationships pursuant to accounting guidance ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em> and, accordingly, changes in fair values of these contracts&#160;are reported in other&#160;income (expense).&#160;There are several risks associated with transactions in options on securities. For example, there are significant differences between the securities and options markets that could result in an imperfect correlation between these markets, causing a given transaction <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to achieve its objectives. A transaction in options or securities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be unsuccessful to some degree because of market behavior or unexpected events. When we write a covered call option, we forgo, during the option&#8217;s life, the opportunity to profit from increases in the market value of the security covering the call option above the sum of the premium and the strike price of the call, but retain the risk of loss should the price of the underlying security decline. The writer of an option has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> control over the time when it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required to fulfill its obligation before the sold option expires, and once an option writer has received an exercise notice, it must deliver the underlying security in exchange for the strike price.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, we did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558880"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559345">not</span></span> own&#160;common shares of any&#160;publicly traded REITs and <ix:nonFraction id="c142558881" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfPubliclyTradedREITsInWhichOptionsAreOwned" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> written covered call options in any of those same REITs.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0px; text-align: justify;">The loan agreement between NetREIT Model, Homes, Inc. (&#8220;NRMH&#8221;) and its lender has a covenant for a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio, (&#8220;FCCR&#8221;) as defined for NRMH as of any date that equals (a) the sum of (i) EBITDA for the period ended as of such date minus (ii) distributions for the period ended as of such date divided by (b) the sum of (ii) principal payments paid for the period ended as of such date plus (iii) interest expense for period ended as of such date.&#160;The FCCR is to be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> less than <ix:nonFraction id="c142558897" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-MortgageNotesMember_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-ModelHomeMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:DebtInstrumentCovenantMinimumFixedChargeCoverageRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.10</ix:nonFraction> to <em style="font: inherit;">1.00,</em> tested at the end of each fiscal quarter.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, NRMH was in compliance with this covenant.&#160;The Company and standalone subsidiaries have&#160;other various quarterly and annual reporting requirements&#160;to the individual property lenders and is in compliance with all material conditions and covenants on those mortgage notes payable as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;with the exception of Dakota Center's loan maturity and Shea Center's DSCR coverage.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">8.</em> NOTES PAYABLE</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 22, 2020, </em>the Company received an Economic Injury Disaster Loan of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558901" contextRef="d_2020-04-22_2020-04-22_DebtInstrumentAxis-EconomicInjuryDisasterLoanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfUnsecuredDebt" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10,000</ix:nonFraction> from the Small Business Administration ("SBA") to provide economic relief during the COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> pandemic. This loan advance is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to be repaid, has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> stipulations on use, and has been recorded as fees and other income in the&#160;consolidated statements of operations during fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2020.</em> On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 17, 2020, </em>we received an additional Economic Injury Disaster Loan ("EIDL") of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558906" contextRef="d_2020-08-17_2020-08-17_DebtInstrumentAxis-EconomicInjuryDisasterLoanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfUnsecuredDebt" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">150,000</ix:nonFraction>, for which principal and interest payments are deferred for <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months from the date of issuance, and interest accrues at <em style="font: inherit;">3.75%</em> per year. The loan matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 17, 2050.&#160;</em>We have used the funds for general corporate purposes to alleviate economic injury caused by&#160;the COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> pandemic, which economic damage included abating or deferring rent to certain tenants (primarily retail tenants).&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the principal balance on SBA loan was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558911" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-EconomicInjuryDisasterLoanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansPayable" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">140,674</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558912" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-EconomicInjuryDisasterLoanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansPayable" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">144,089</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">During&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> we had&#160;issued <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> promissory note&#160;to our majority owned subsidiary,&#160;Dubose Model Home Investors <em style="font: inherit;">202</em> LP, for the refinancing of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> model home property&#160;in Texas, for approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558917" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-PromissoryNoteForRefinancingOneModelHomeMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-MajorityOwnedSubsidiaryDuboseModelHomeInvestors202LPAnd204LPMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million with an interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c142558918" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-PromissoryNoteForRefinancingOneModelHomeMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-MajorityOwnedSubsidiaryDuboseModelHomeInvestors202LPAnd204LPMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.55</ix:nonFraction>% per annum and original maturity date&#160;of <em style="font: inherit;"> August 15, 2024, </em>which was extended for another year with an interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c142558919" contextRef="i_2024-08-15_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-PromissoryNoteForRefinancingOneModelHomeMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-MajorityOwnedSubsidiaryDuboseModelHomeInvestors202LPAnd204LPMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">8.0</ix:nonFraction>% per annum. This note&#160;payable and note&#160;receivable, including interest expense and interest income related to this&#160;promissory note, is eliminated through consolidation on our financial statements.&#160;This property was subsequently sold in <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2024, </em>and the loan was paid in full.&#160;As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> other notes payable.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Litigation. </i></b>From time to time, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>become involved in various lawsuits or legal proceedings which arise in the ordinary course of business. Neither the Company nor any of the Company's properties are presently subject to any material litigation nor, to the Company's knowledge, is there any material threatened litigation.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Environmental matters. </i></b>The Company monitors its properties for the presence of hazardous or toxic substances. While there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that a material environmental liability does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exist, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently aware of any environmental liability with respect to the properties that would have a material effect on the Company's financial condition, results of operations and cash flow. Further, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> aware of any environmental liability or any unasserted claim or assessment with respect to an environmental liability that the Company believes would require additional disclosure or recording of a loss contingency.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Financial Markets.</i></b>&#160;The Company monitors concerns over economic recession,&#160;interest rate increases, policy priorities of the U.S. presidential administration, trade wars, labor shortages, and inflation, any of which&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>contribute to increased volatility and diminished expectations for the economy and markets. Additionally, the economic and geopolitical ramifications of the military conflicts in the&#160;Middle East&#160;and&#160;Ukraine, including sanctions, retaliatory sanctions, nationalism, supply chain disruptions and other consequences,&#160;could impact commercial real estate fundamentals and result in lower occupancy, lower rental rates, and declining values in our real estate portfolio and in the collateral securing our loan investments. We have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently experienced a direct material impact to our Company or operations; however, we will continue to monitor the financial markets for events that could impact our commercial real estate properties.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Preferred Stock.&#160;</i></b>The Company is authorized to issue up to <ix:nonFraction id="c142558951" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of Preferred Stock (the &#8220;Preferred Stock&#8221;).    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 20, 2024, </em>the Company&#160;entered into an underwriting agreement&#160;with The Benchmark Company, LLC,&#160;pursuant to which the Company issued and sold in an underwritten public offering <ix:nonFraction id="c142558962" contextRef="d_2024-06-20_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">109,054</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s Series D Preferred Stock.&#160;The shares of Series D Preferred Stock were sold to the public at a price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558963" contextRef="i_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">16.00</ix:nonFraction> per share. The Company agreed to an underwriting discount of <ix:nonFraction id="c142558964" contextRef="i_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:EquityOfferingUnderwritingDiscountPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">7</ix:nonFraction>% of the public offering price of the shares of Series D Preferred Stock sold in the offering. The offering closed on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 24, 2024, </em>generating gross proceeds of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558965" contextRef="d_2024-06-20_2024-06-24_CounterpartyNameAxis-TheBenchmarkCompanyLlcMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-UnderwrittenPublicOfferingMember" unitRef="USD" name="sqft:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfPreferredStockAndPreferenceStockGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.74</ix:nonFraction> million, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses payable by the Company. The Company has used the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate and working capital purposes, including the acquisition of&#160;additional properties.&#160;Below are some of the key terms of the Series D Preferred Stock:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Dividends:</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Holders of shares of the Series D Preferred Stock are entitled to receive cumulative cash dividends at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c142558966" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">9.375</ix:nonFraction>% per annum of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558967" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockLiquidationPreference" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">25.00</ix:nonFraction> per share liquidation preference (equivalent to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558968" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePerDollarAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.34375</ix:nonFraction> per annum per share). Dividends will be payable monthly on the <em style="font: inherit;">15th</em> day of each month (each, a &#8220;Dividend Payment Date&#8221;), provided that if any Dividend Payment Date is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a business day, then the dividend that would otherwise have been payable on that Dividend Payment Date <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be paid on the next succeeding business day without adjustment in the amount of the dividend.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Voting Rights:</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Holders of shares of the Series D Preferred Stock will generally have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> voting rights. However, if the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> pay dividends on the Series D Preferred Stock for <em style="font: inherit;">eighteen</em> or more monthly dividend periods (whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consecutive), the holders of the Series D Preferred Stock (voting separately as a class with the holders of all other classes or series of the Company&#8217;s preferred stock it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue upon which like voting rights have been conferred and are exercisable and which are entitled to vote as a class with the Series D Preferred Stock in the election referred to below) will be entitled to vote for the election of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558975">two</span> additional directors to serve on the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors until the Company pays, or declares and sets apart funds for the payment of, all dividends that it owes on the Series D Preferred Stock, subject to certain limitations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In addition, the affirmative vote of the holders of at least <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142558976">two</span>-thirds of the outstanding shares of Series D Preferred Stock (voting together as a class with all other series of parity preferred stock the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue upon which like voting rights have been conferred and are exercisable) is required at any time for the Company to (i) authorize or issue any class or series of its stock ranking senior to the Series D Preferred Stock with respect to the payment of dividends or the distribution of assets on liquidation, dissolution or winding up or (ii) to amend any provision of the Company charter so as to materially and adversely affect any rights of the Series D Preferred Stock or to take certain other actions.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Liquidation Preference</i>:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the event of the Company&#8217;s voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up, the holders of shares of Series D Preferred Stock will be entitled to be paid out of the assets the Company has legally available for distribution to its stockholders, subject to the preferential rights of the holders of any class or series of its stock the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue ranking senior to the Series D Preferred Stock with respect to the distribution of assets upon liquidation, dissolution or winding up, a liquidation preference of <em style="font: inherit;">$25.00</em> per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends to, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> including, the date of payment, before any distribution of assets is made to holders of the Company&#8217;s common stock or any other class or series of the Company&#8217;s stock it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue that ranks junior to the Series D Preferred Stock as to liquidation rights.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the event that, upon any such voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up, the Company&#8217;s available assets are insufficient to pay the amount of the liquidating distributions on all outstanding shares of Series D Preferred Stock and the corresponding amounts payable on all shares of other classes or series of the Company&#8217;s stock that it issues ranking on parity with the Series D Preferred Stock in the distribution of assets, then the holders of the Series D Preferred Stock and all other such classes or series of stock shall share ratably in any such distribution of assets in proportion to the full liquidating distributions to which they would otherwise be respectively entitled.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Redemption:</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Commencing on or after <em style="font: inherit;"> June 15, 2026, </em>the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>redeem, at its option, the Series D Preferred Stock, in whole or in part, at a cash redemption price equal to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558979" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockRedemptionPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">25.00</ix:nonFraction> per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends to, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> including&#160;the redemption date. Prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 15, 2026, </em>upon a Change of Control (as defined in the&#160;Articles Supplementary), the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>redeem, at its option, the Series D Preferred Stock, in whole or part, at a cash redemption price of <em style="font: inherit;">$25.00</em> per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends to, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> including the redemption date. The Series D Preferred Stock has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> stated maturity, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be subject to any sinking fund or other mandatory redemption, and will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be convertible into or exchangeable for any of our other securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In accordance with the terms of the Series D Preferred Stock, the Series D monthly dividend has been approved by the Board of Directors through <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558986" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DividendsAxis-O2024H2DividendsMember_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendsPerShareDeclared" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.19531</ix:nonFraction> per share payable on the <em style="font: inherit;">15th</em>&#160;of every month to stockholders of record of Series D Preferred Stock as of the last day of the prior month.&#160;Total&#160;dividends paid to Series D Preferred stockholders during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;were&#160;approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142558989" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfDividends" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142558990" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfDividends" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Effective on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 19, 2025, </em>the Company amended its charter by filing Articles of Amendment with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation of Maryland in order to effect a <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-for-<ix:nonFraction id="c142559027" contextRef="d_2025-05-19_2025-05-19_NonmonetaryTransactionTypeAxis-ReverseStockSplitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteStockSplitConversionRatio1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction> reverse stock split of its outstanding shares of common stock (the &#8220;Reverse Stock Split&#8221;). As a result of the Reverse Stock Split, every <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock issued or outstanding were automatically reclassified into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> new share of common stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559030" contextRef="i_2025-05-19" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.10</ix:nonFraction> per share, subject to the treatment of fractional shares as described below, without any action on the part of the holders. All historical share and per-share amounts reflected throughout the accompanying consolidated financial statements and other financial information in this Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K&#160;have been retroactively adjusted to reflect the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Reverse Stock Split as if the split occurred as of the earliest period presented. The Reverse Stock Split did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affect the number of authorized shares of common stock. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> fractional shares were issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Stockholders who would otherwise have been entitled to receive fractional shares as a result of the Reverse Stock Split were rounded up to the nearest whole share. All equity awards and warrants outstanding immediately prior to the Reverse Stock Split were proportionately adjusted to reflect the Reverse Stock Split. Effective immediately after the Reverse Stock Split, the Company decreased the par value of the shares of Series A Common Stock from $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559035" contextRef="i_2025-05-18_StatementClassOfStockAxis-CommonClassAMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.10</ix:nonFraction> per share back to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559036" contextRef="i_2025-05-19_StatementClassOfStockAxis-CommonClassAMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.01</ix:nonFraction> per share.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 8, 2025, </em>we commenced the increase the number of shares accepted for payment in the Tender Offer by up to <ix:nonFraction id="c142559091" contextRef="i_2025-04-08_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-FixedPriceSelftenderOfferMember" applicable withholding taxes and without interest.&#160;The Tender Offer expired at <em style="font: inherit;">11:59</em> P.M., New York City time, on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 5, 2025. </em>Based on the final count by the depositary for the Tender Offer, <ix:nonFraction id="c142559095" contextRef="i_2025-05-05_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-FixedPriceSelftenderOfferMember" defects. Pursuant to the terms of the Tender Offer, the Company accepted for purchase <ix:nonFraction id="c142559097" contextRef="i_2025-05-05_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-FixedPriceSelftenderOfferMember" unitRef="Share" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramNumberOfSharesAuthorizedToBeRepurchased" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">214,412</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of Series A common stock, including <ix:nonFraction id="c142559098" contextRef="i_2025-05-05_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-FixedPriceSelftenderOfferMember" unitRef="Share" name="sqft:StockRepurchaseProgramOddLotShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,209</ix:nonFraction>&#160;odd lot shares. Total cash required to complete the Tender Offer was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559099" contextRef="i_2025-05-05_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-FixedPriceSelftenderOfferMember" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,458,000</ix:nonFraction>, excluding fees and expenses related to the Tender Offer.&#160;We believe that the tender offer provided an efficient mechanism to provide our stockholders who desired immediate liquidity with the opportunity to tender shares at a favorable price relative to the current market price and without incurring broker&#8217;s fees associated with most secondary market sales, while also providing a benefit to those stockholders who did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> participate, as such stockholders automatically increased their relative percentage ownership interest in the Company and our future operations, including any liquidity events that we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have in the future.&#160;Another purpose of the Tender Offer was to reduce the number of our issued and outstanding shares and to reduce or eliminate all of our odd lots.&#160;Overall, we believe that the Tender Offer was a prudent use of our financial resources given our business profile, capital structure, assets and liabilities.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Cash Dividends. </i></b>For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160; <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559101"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559360">not</span></span> declare and pay a Series A Common Stock cash dividend.&#160;For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, the Company declared and paid Series D Preferred Stock&#160;cash dividends of approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142559102" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfDividends" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559103" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfDividends" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.&#160;The Company intends&#160;to continue to pay dividends to our common stockholders on a quarterly basis, and on a monthly basis to holders of our&#160;Series D Preferred Stock&#160;going forward, but there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> guarantee the Board of Directors will approve any future dividends.&#160;The following is a summary of distributions declared per share of our Series A Common Stock and for our Series D Preferred Stock&#160;for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 28, 2026, </em>the&#160;Board of Directors has suspended the Company&#8217;s monthly dividend on its Series D Preferred Stock commencing with the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>monthly dividend that would have been paid on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 15, 2026. </em>In accordance with the terms of the Series D Preferred Stock, the unpaid monthly dividends will continue to accrue at $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559105" contextRef="d_2026-01-28_2026-01-28_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesDPreferredStockMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePerDollarAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.19531</ix:nonFraction> per share each month.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No</em> interest, or sum of money in lieu of interest, is payable in respect of any dividend payments on the Series D Preferred Stock that are in arrears.&#160; The Board and the Company intend to reassess, on a quarterly basis, when accrued dividends on the Series D Preferred Stock <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be paid and when the monthly dividend payments can be reinstated.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><b>Partnership Interests.&#160;</b></i>Through the Company, its subsidiaries, and its partnerships, we own&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142559108" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-CommercialPropertyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRealEstateProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction> commercial properties in fee interest,&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559109">two</span> of which we own partial interests in through our holdings in various affiliates in which we serve as general partner, member and/or manager. Each of the limited partnerships is referred to as a &#8220;DownREIT.&#8221; In each DownREIT, we have the right, through put and call options, to require our co-investors to exchange their interests for shares of our Common Stock at a stated price after a defined period (generally <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years from the date they <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> invested in the entity&#8217;s real property), the occurrence of a specified event or a combination thereof. The Company is a limited partner in <ix:nonFraction id="c142559112" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="sqft:NumberOfLimitedPartnershipsInWhichCompanyIsSoleGeneralPartner" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">five</ix:nonFraction> partnerships and sole stockholder in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> corporation, which entities purchase and lease&#160;model homes from homebuilders.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">12.</em> SHARE-BASED INCENTIVE PLAN</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt;">The Company maintains a restricted stock incentive plan for the purpose of attracting and retaining officers, employees, and non-employee board members. Share awards generally vest in equal annual installments over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559115">three</span>-to-<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559116">ten</span> year period from date of issuance. Non-vested shares have voting rights and are eligible for any dividends paid on shares of common stock. The Company recognized compensation cost for these fixed awards over the service vesting period, which represents the requisite service period, using the straight-line method. Prior to our IPO, the value of non-vested shares was calculated based on the offering price of the shares in the most recent private placement offering of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559117" contextRef="i_2006-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">20.00</ix:nonFraction>, adjusted for stock dividends since granted and assumed selling costs, which management believed approximated fair market value as of the date of grant. Upon our IPO, the value of non-vested shares granted is generally calculated based on the closing price of our common stock on the date of the grant.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">During our Annual Meeting of Stockholders, held on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2023, </em>the Company's <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Incentive Award Plan was amended to increase the available shares for issuance from <ix:nonFraction id="c142559119" contextRef="i_2022-05-26_PlanNameAxis-The2017IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">250,000</ix:nonFraction> to <ix:nonFraction id="c142559120" contextRef="i_2023-06-01_PlanNameAxis-The2017IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">350,000</ix:nonFraction> and add an evergreen provision to, on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 1</em><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">st</sup> and <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1</em><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">st</sup> of each year, automatically increase the maximum number of shares of common stock available under the plan to <em style="font: inherit;">15%</em> of the Company's outstanding shares of common stock, if on such date <em style="font: inherit;">350,000</em> (as adjusted for any reverse splits) is less than <em style="font: inherit;">15%</em> of the Company's then-outstanding shares of common stock.&#160; At the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Annual Meeting of Stockholders, held on <em style="font: inherit;"> June&#160; </em><em style="font: inherit;">2,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Incentive Award Plan was amended and restated to (i) increase the number of shares available for issuance thereunder to <ix:nonFraction id="c142559128" contextRef="i_2025-06-02_PlanNameAxis-The2017IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">450,000</ix:nonFraction> from <em style="font: inherit;">350,000</em> shares of common stock and (ii) revise the plan&#8217;s evergreen provision to, on <em style="font: inherit;"> April </em><em style="font: inherit;">1st</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> October </em><em style="font: inherit;">1st</em> of each year, automatically increase the maximum number of shares of common stock available under the plan to <em style="font: inherit;">15%</em> of the Company&#8217;s outstanding shares of common stock, if on such date <em style="font: inherit;">450,000</em> shares constitute less than <em style="font: inherit;">15%</em> of the Company&#8217;s then-outstanding shares of common stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Share-based compensation expense was approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142559141" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559142" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;for the&#160;years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively, as part of our general and administrative&#160;costs.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em><i>,</i> future unrecognized stock compensation related to unvested shares totaled approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142559144" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.9</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3148008" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">13.</em>&#160;SEGMENTS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s reportable segments consist of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142559146">three</span> types of real estate properties for which the Company&#8217;s chief operating decision maker (CODM), which is our Chief Executive Officer ("CEO"), as the CEO has the final decision when allocating capital and personnel to the various segments,&#160;internally&#160;evaluate operating performance and financial results: Office/Industrial Properties, Model Home Properties and Retail Properties. The Company also has certain corporate-level activities including accounting, finance, legal administration, and management information systems which are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered separate operating segments.&#160;There is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material inter-segment activity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The CODM evaluates the performance of our&#160;segments based upon an internal net operating income (&#8220;NOI&#8221;), which is a non-GAAP supplemental financial measure on a quarterly basis as disclosed in the <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Qs and <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Ks. We believe that NOI is a widely accepted measure of comparative operating performance in the real estate community. However, our use of the term NOI <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be comparable to that of other real estate companies as they <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have different methodologies for computing this amount.&#160;The Company defines NOI for its segments as operating revenues (rental income, tenant reimbursements, parking income, and other operating income, net of provision for bad debt) less rental operating costs (property operating expenses, real estate taxes, insurance, utilities, repairs and maintenance, and asset management fees) excluding interest expense. NOI excludes certain items that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered to be controllable in connection with the management of an asset such as non-property income &amp; expenses, depreciation &amp; amortization, real estate acquisition fees &amp; expenses, non-cash impairments and corporate general &amp; administrative expenses. Quarterly the Company reviews and test for non-cash impairments, as required by GAAP, on all our properties (i.e. Office/Industrial Properties,&#160;Retail Properties, and Model Home&#160;Properties); however, the CODM does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consider those non-cash impairments with evaluating the segment&#8217;s cash operations and NOI.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The CODM uses NOI to evaluate and assess each segments' performance and in deciding how to allocate resources.&#160;For Model Home performance the CODM also includes the gain or loss on sale of real estate assets net of any impairments, because we believe that is a major component in the operating success of the segment and part of the business model for Model Homes.&#160;The gain on sale of model homes resulted in cash flows to the Company that the CODM can decide on how to allocate to future operations.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The following tables compare the Company&#8217;s segment activity and NOI and adjusted NOI for Model Home income&#160;to its results of operations and financial position as of and for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.&#160;The line items listed in the below NOI tables include the significant expense considered by the CODM for cash allocations on future investments.&#160;The Other Non-Segment &amp; Consolidating Items represent corporate activity, the investment in Conduit Pharmaceutical, and other eliminating items for consolidation.&#160;The information for Corporate and Other are presented to reconcile back to the consolidated statement of operations, but is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered a reportable segment.&#160;This includes the loss on Conduit marketable securities.</p>
